rationale.conceptual: The underlying DFT/NEB methodology is well-documented and widely used in computational chemistry/materials science. However, correctly setting up a surface slab, identifying adsorption sites, constructing diffusion paths for NEB, and deriving electrochemical quantities (capacity, voltage) requires non-trivial domain knowledge and careful implementation of multiple interacting components (slab relaxation, adsorption, barrier searches, sequential coverage). Not a purely textbook recipe, but not a novel custom method.
rationale.execution: The workflow involves ~6-8 sequential DFT stages: slab relaxation, four single-Li adsorption calculations, two surface NEB paths, one surface-to-bulk NEB path, and multiple sequential adsorption calculations up to LiₓNiO. Each stage must be set up, run, and post-processed, requiring handling of input files, potential job scheduling, and extraction of energies and barriers. This multi-stage pipeline with dependencies is moderately complex but not a fragile 7+ stage orchestration; all input data (crystal structure, pseudopotentials) are standard.

difficulty.reasoning: The task is a standard computational materials science DFT study: build a surface slab, compute adsorption energies at high-symmetry sites, run CI-NEB for diffusion barriers, and derive capacity and voltage. The method is well-established (PBE+PAW, NEB) and the pipeline has moderate complexity with about 6-8 DFT runs, but no algorithmic novelty. Resource needs are modest CPU-only, small slab size.
